text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Singapore and Thailand can seek ways to add value to each other's strengths, even as both develop their ports, information technology networks and industries, said Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and Trade and Industry Minister Lee Yock Suan.
- The Indonesian armed forces (Abri) are running out of patience with the mob violence in East Java and has warned that rioters will be shot on sight to quell further unrest.
- U.S.-listed bookstore chain Borders Group Inc is to open its first overseas outlet at Wheelock Place mail in Orchard Road by the end of the year.

- DBS Land completed its purchase of a 19.16 percent stake in Parkway and is closer to a takeover, say sources who claim it has settled on a price for the Ang family's 13.5 percent stake in the health care group.
- Malaysia's central bank has rejected applications by MBf Capital and Suria Capital Holdings to start merger and acquisition talks, according to separate statements from the companies.

- The Thai baht exploded in offshore markets to a high not seen in almost 15 years, as speculators continued to be squeezed by the Bank of Thailand's measures blocking their access to the domestic market.
- Thai stocks fell to their lowest levels in eight years, with the Stock Exchange of Thailand index sinking below the 500 mark, less than half its level nine months ago.
- Malaysia's Renong group is undertaking the feasibility study for the proposed bridge across the busy Straits of Malacca to link Malaysia and Sumatra, sources said in Kuala Lumpur.
- Singapore companies are keen to invest in port facilities, power plants, financial institutions and property in Thailand as they view the current weakness of the country's economy as temporary.
- Property developer Wing Tai Holdings intends to spend Singapore $235 million expanding its service apartment business in the next three years.

- Main board listed Wing Tai Holdings is promising subscribers to its five-year redeemable convertible cumulative preference shares (RCCPS) an approximate redemption price of US$1,300, or an annual rate of return of 6.25 to 6.75 percent. The issue price of each RCCPS will be about US$1,000.
- Ho Wah Genting International substantial shareholder Tang Tsung Chin has sold his entire 14.9 percent stake held through Happy Theme Sdn Bhd.

- News Corp and Air New Zealand may reduce their half shares in Australian carrier Ansett to sell Singapore Airlines an equal third stake worth AUD$200 million to AUD$300 million, a newspaper report said.
- Major Guthrie shareholder Endang Utari Mokodompit announced the sale of a substantial stake in Guthrie GTS through Crownhill Holdings, which the Indonesian businesswoman controls.
- Buoyed by expectations of a recovering chip industry, equipment maker Advanced Systems Automation is "seriously considering" setting up factories in Korea and Taiwan.
